newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Mixed deals struck in FTSE, volume light.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Mixed deals struck in FTSE, volume light.

text.p: Trading activity in UK equity options was light on Thursday as many traders preferred to wait for the outcome of today's national election before dealing in size, dealers said.

There was mixed trading FTSE options and some of the main deals were the purchase of out-of-the-money calls or the sale of out-of-the-money puts which will make money if the election result causes the market to race ahead.
In the near-term month, one such deal was the buying of 300 May 4300 calls in FTSE at 4p. Another was the sale of 250 May 4300 puts at 12-1/2p.
There was also a seller of 1,000 May 4550 calls at 16p.
Of the larger deals in European style FTSE one was a reverse calendar spread in which 500 June 4325 puts were sold at 43p and 500 September 4325 puts bought at 90p for a net credit of 47p.

The more volatile the market becomes up to June expiry the more the current 47p spread will reduce and the position can then be closed at a profit. If after June expiry the short puts are still held, the market needs to stay above 4325 by September expiry for additional profits.
By 1340 GMT, the FTSE was up 4.0 at 4440.0.

Over in stock options one large deal was in property company Land Securities where a strangle was bought. This involved buying 250 January 750 puts at 18p and 250 January 850 puts at calls at 27p. A large movemment by the underlying shares will make this trade profitable. The shares gained 4p to 805p.
In conglomerate BTR, 200 November 300 calls were sold at 5p and in pharmaceuticals group SmithKline Beecham 225 July 900 puts were bought at 11p.
BTR slipped a penny to 251-1/2p and SmithKline Beecham was p 1/2p weaker at 991p.
